headline: Set special election date to February 2, 2027, approved $183,000 ride share transfer, and referred 276 Broadway land purchase to public hearing.
summary: The Council held public hearings on four Boston Gas main projects and referred them to the Wire Inspector. It voted down a motion on inactive voter legislation, referred several councilor requests to the City Manager, appointed three people to the Lowell Youth Commission, and adopted a $1,000 gift, a special election schedule moved to February 2, 2027, a contract with TRC Environmental Corp., and a $183,000 transfer for Ride Share. The Council also referred several citizen petitions to city departments and entered executive session to discuss HCID Parcel 15 negotiations, security cameras, and a potential TIF agreement with the Lowell Housing Authority.
decisions: Referred Boston Gas's request to relocate a gas main on Stockbridge Avenue to the Wire Inspector for report and recommendation.
Referred Boston Gas's request to replace gas mains along Lawrence and Woburn Streets to the Wire Inspector.
Referred Boston Gas's request to replace gas mains on Leroy, Canal and Grove Streets to the Wire Inspector.
Referred Boston Gas's request to replace gas mains on Llewellyen, Beacon, Third and Bennett Streets to the Wire Inspector.
Failed a motion asking the City Manager to contact Lowell's state delegation about legislation on inactive voters, 4 yeas to 5 nays.
Referred to the City Manager a request for a report on implementation of the state law on inactive voters and voter education.
Referred to the City Manager a request for an update on installing Cambodian Town banners along Middlesex Street.
Referred to the City Manager and City Clerk a request to offer language support and interpretation services at public meetings.
Referred to the City Manager a request to explore options for increasing compliance with the noise ordinance for dumpster services.
Referred to the City Manager a request to explore adding a skatepark in Centralville, including possible locations.
Referred to the City Manager a request to explore a land co-op model to increase affordable homeownership.
Referred to the City Manager a request to ask tax-exempt partners such as ULowell, MCC, and LHA for voluntary help preventing fire department brownouts.
Referred to the City Manager a request to start the process to fill the vacant District 1 City Council seat.
Appointed Dylan Quinones, Avry McKiernan, and Ariana Martinez to the Lowell Youth Commission.
Adopted acceptance of a $1,000 gift from the Demoulas Foundation, 9 yeas to 0, 1 absent.
Adopted the Special Election Schedule as amended, moving the election date from December 15, 2026, to February 2, 2027, 6 yeas.
Adopted a contract with TRC Environmental Corp., 9 yeas to 0, 1 absent.
Adopted a $183,000 transfer for Ride Share, 9 yeas to 0, 1 absent.
Withdrew a proposed $43,000 salary transfer from the agenda.
Referred the loan order for land acquisition at 276 Broadway for a Senior Center to a public hearing on October 20, 2026.
Accepted and adopted Wire Inspector orders for National Grid on South Highland Street and Boston Gas main replacements on Aiken, Dalton, Exeter, and Fulton Streets.
Referred six property damage claims to the Law Department for report and recommendation.
Referred Michael Malvesti's request for sidewalk infrastructure on Acropolis Road to the Transportation Engineer.
Referred Sokmey Phe's request for a 15 Minute parking sign at 89 Loring Street to the Transportation Engineer.
Referred Kennith Harkins' request regarding the condition of the City cemetery to the City Manager.
Referred Yolanda Irizarry's request for a handicap parking sign at 33 4th Street to the Transportation Engineer.
Referred Phillip Fryns' request for a handicap parking sign at 55 London Street to the Transportation Engineer.

Voted to enter executive session to discuss HCID Parcel 15 negotiations, security deployment including Flock cameras, and a potential TIF agreement with the Lowell Housing Authority, 9 yeas to 0, 1 absent.

5. CITY COUNCIL - MOTIONS
5.1. C. Nuon - Req. City Mgr. contact Lowell's state delegation to 
advocate for legislation to no longer make a voter inactive if they miss
the annual municipal census form.
In City Council, seconded by C. McDonough, failed per Roll Call vote 4 
yeas (M. Gitschier, C. Liang, C. McDonough, C. Nuon), 5 nays (C. 
Descoteaux, C. Juran, C. Mercier, C. Robinson, C. Scott), 1 absent (C. 
Chau).  So voted.  C. Nuon noted legislation gave election directors a 
different means to move voters to the active list through a post office data 
base.  C. Nuon suggested sending a letter of support to delegation 
supporting proposed legislation.  C. Juran noted she had not seen the bills 
and that there could be some issues and concerns regarding the use of the 
post office.  C. Scott noted concern on how it would work and a lot is not 
known about the process.  C. Mercier noted her reservations and that the 
focus should be prevention of fraud.  C. Nuon stated that the failure to fill 
out census form should not be a reason to remove voters from the roll.  C. 
Robinson recognized the spirit of the motion but noted the other means to 
be placed back on the voter rolls.  C. McDonough noted the need for a 
better process but was not sure how this would work.
